summary: Weekly POC sync focused on cost/unit economics. Redwood and Quantaco reviewed tokens/sec per dollar across model variants, observed caching savings for prefix-heavy workloads, and discussed batching tradeoffs vs latency. Action items: run caching on/off benchmarks, share updated cost spreadsheets, and align on production traffic profile. Follow-up scheduled for next week.
transcript: 00:00:00 - Sana: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. we'll give it a few more secs, hi Olivia, Marcus, Priya, can you hear us?
00:00:08 - Olivia: Yep, loud and clear. Sorry, ran a tiny bit late here.
00:00:12 - Marco: Hi team, Marco from Redwood SE. Today we'll focus on cost economics — tokens per second per dollar and how caching and batching move the needle.
00:00:23 - Marcus: Sounds good. we want to understand where our biggest wins are. right now our throughput requirements are... um about 200 qps peak, average maybe 80 qps.
00:00:35 - Priya: And most requests are relatively short, but we do have a subset of long conversations that keep KV state, so caching could help there.
00:00:45 - Sana: Quick agenda: 1) recapping last week's perf runs; 2) cost model walkthrough; 3) caching & batching tradeoffs; 4) action items.

00:00:57 - Marco: I'll share screen — rough numbers from the bench. we tested small-llama-13B and quantized-13B-8bit. tokens/sec measured on our dedicated pool: baseline no batching 45 tokens/sec on 13B int8, with continuous batching at 16 request batch got to 240 tokens/sec.
00:01:24 - Olivia: Wait, 240 tokens/sec at batch=16? that seems high — is that tokens/sec per GPU or per deployment?

00:01:32 - Marco: Per GPU in our test harness. real-world will vary. the important metric we computed was tokens per dollar, so we normalized by GPU-hour cost. baseline gave us about 120k tokens per $1 for the quantized profile, batching pushed that to ~640k tokens per $1 — roughly 5x improvement.
00:02:02 - Priya: 5x is a lot. but what's the latency impact at tail? our app needs p95 under 500ms for interactive features.

00:02:12 - Marco: Good call. batching increases tail latency; at batch16 p95 went from 220ms to 680ms for single-turn prompts. for conversations with KV caching enabled, effective latency for cached prefixes is much lower because we avoid re-computing the prefix — that was the other big win.
00:02:36 - Marcus: Can you explain the caching numbers again? our prefix-heavy users are maybe 20% of traffic but account for 50% of tokens.

00:02:44 - Marco: Sure. Our KV/prefix cache avoids recomputing stored key-values for repeated prefixes. in the run with caching on, total tokens processed by the model dropped by ~38% for your trace, translating to around 35% cost savings. the tokens/sec/$ metric improved from 120k to 185k in the unbatched case and from 640k to ~850k in batched runs.
00:03:12 - Olivia: Those savings hinge on cache hit rate, right? what's assumed here?

00:03:18 - Marco: We used an empirical hit rate from the traces you shared — about 46% reuse on prefixes. if hit rate drops to 20% the improvement falls to single-digit percent. so we need your real traffic traces to finalize numbers.
00:03:32 - Priya: We can share anonymized traces. small ask: include sequence length distribution plus session stickiness. we'll get that by Friday.

00:03:41 - Sana: Great. another point — quantization. moving to 8-bit int profile reduces per-token latency slightly and cuts cost per GPU hour since we can pack more in a node. did you want to comment Marco?

00:03:54 - Marco: Yeah, quantization reduces memory footprint so throughput improves. on our GPU infra, int8 path gave ~12% better tokens/sec for same batch size compared to float16. but we did see a 1-2% drop in accuracy on a small eval — needs validation by your QA.
00:04:13 - Olivia: That accuracy hit is concerning for certain workflows; we'll pair with the eval team. but cost-wise it seems promising.
00:04:20 - Marcus: On batching tradeoffs — can we do adaptive batching? when latency requirement tightens we lower batch size?

00:04:27 - Marco: Yes, Redwood supports dynamic batching policies: latency-first routing for VIP traffic and throughput pooling for low-priority. you can set policy by route or token budget. tradeoffs are inevitable — higher batching improves tokens/$ but increases p95.
00:04:43 - Priya: Any rule-of-thumb for batch size? we don't want to test every combo.

00:04:48 - Marco: Rule: for sub-500ms p95 target, keep effective batch size under 8 for your current model & infra. for throughput-heavy offline workloads batch 32+ is fine. also consider prefix caching which lets you keep small batch sizes but still get savings.
00:05:05 - Olivia: Can you share the spreadsheet model now?
00:05:07 - Sana: I'll drop the updated cost model in Slack after the call — includes tokens/sec/$, GPU cost assumptions, and sensitivity to cache hit rate and batch size.
00:05:15 - Marcus: One question about the GPU pricing you used — is that our cloud list price or Redwood dedicated amortized cost?

00:05:22 - Marco: For the model we used an amortized dedicated rate (Midwest us-east equivalent) with 730 hours month and included overhead. Sana will put both cloud-on-demand and dedicated amortized in the sheet.
00:05:34 - Priya: Another practical: can the cache survive restarts? we have autoscaling and sometimes nodes cycle.

00:05:40 - Marco: Cache is logical at the serving layer and can be backed by Redis in Dedicated— survives warm restarts if configured; on Hosted there is sticky node-level caching with TTL and fallback. we can propose the setup in the design doc.
00:05:56 - Olivia: Good. also curious about cold-start costs when traffic spikes — if caching helps ramp up quicker?

00:06:02 - Marco: Caching primarily reduces compute for repeated prefixes; it doesn't reduce cold-start instance spinup. for spikes, we recommend a small warm pool + burst policy to avoid cold-start latency spikes.

00:06:14 - Sana: quick recap of the numbers we saw: unbatched int8 gave ~120k tokens/$, batch16 gave ~640k tokens/$, caching at 46% hit raised those to ~185k and ~850k respectively. we flagged p95 latencies 220ms -> 680ms at batch16.
00:06:31 - Marcus: If we target p95 400ms, what batch size should we aim for?
00:06:36 - Marco: around batch8 was close — p95 around 360-420ms depending on prompt mix. with caching you can keep batch8 and hit throughput targets for a lot of traffic patterns.
00:06:47 - Priya: For the benchmark runs you want us to provide traffic profile and a smaller eval set, correct?
00:06:52 - Marco: Yes please — real request traces, anonymized. also indicate which routes are latency-sensitive vs throughput-first.
00:06:59 - Olivia: We'll compile that. one operational concern — audit logs and data retention for PII. are cached KV entries considered sensitive?

00:07:08 - Marco: Great point. Redwood's cache can be configured to exclude sensitive fields; we also support encryption at rest and KMS for Private deployments. for Hosted we'll surface retention controls and redaction hooks. I'll include the security doc link.
00:07:24 - Sana: I'll attach the SOC2/ISO summary and the cache config doc after the call.
00:07:29 - Olivia: Awesome. any competitor reasons we should be aware of? Marcus asked earlier about Anthropic pricing — did you benchmark against them?

00:07:35 - Marco: We did a quick apples-to-oranges run, Anthropic endpoints had lower throughput for equivalent latency in our tests but better out-of-the-box safety for some workloads. OpenAI was costlier on tokens/$ in sustained throughput scenarios. we'll include a short note in the follow-up.
00:07:50 - Priya: One more: can Redwood show per-route cost in the console so we can attribute spends?
00:07:55 - Sana: Yes, Redwood Console gives per-route token and cost breakouts, and you can filter by model and time windows.
00:08:02 - Marcus: Great. timeline-wise — after you run the caching on/off benchmarks, what's the next step?

00:08:08 - Marco: We'll analyze and add sensitivity columns to the cost sheet. then recommend a production config: model variant, quantization profile, batching policy, and cache TTLs. ideally pilot for two weeks on a small percent of traffic.
00:08:21 - Olivia: Pilot sounds good. Priya and I will sync offline and pick the first 5% of traffic to route.
00:08:27 - Sana: Perfect. I'll send the sheet and links. Next meeting set for 2026-03-25 at same time to review numbers.
00:08:36 - Priya: thanks all, that was helpful.
00:08:38 - Sana: thanks everyone. action items we'll paste into the CRM and slack. bye.
00:08:42 - (call ends)
